page: Amazon Web Services r5.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache. It provides 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, establishing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI. The server does not bundle local disk storage or GPUs, relying on remote network volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the compute constraints of the single-core topology alongside standard memory capabilities. In multi-threaded evaluations, stress-ng recorded 1,675.39 and Geekbench multi-core scored 1,205.0, reflecting performance characteristics typical of low-core count allocations. PassMark CPU reached 1,997.34, with extended instructions scoring 1,417.71. Memory subsystem tests showed 13.27 GB/s read throughput and 11.46 GB/s write throughput on large 256 MB blocks, while PassMark memory recorded 1,641.47. In application-level benchmarks, the instance completed 1.64 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved 1.86 GB/s of static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, r5.large provides a low-barrier deployment option for workloads requiring a substantial memory footprint relative to processing capacity. While multi-threaded compute throughput is bounded by the physical single-core limit, the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio avoids paying for unneeded processor cores. This balance fits applications such as in-memory data caching, Redis or Memcached tiers, small relational database instances, background worker queues, and mid-tier backend services with high RAM requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.large is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz, it supplies 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration includes AVX-512 vector support, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local storage, and no GPU hardware. Synthetic testing demonstrates modest compute performance consistent with its core count, including a PassMark CPU score of 1,997.34 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1,205.0. Memory throughput yields 13.27 GB/s for large-block reads and 1.64 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers cost-effective memory density for memory-bound, compute-light workloads such as caching layers, Redis nodes, and small relational databases.
